text: We tested whether restricting the student's fine-tune to a low-rank adapter (LoRA rank 16) changes weak-to-strong generalization, using qwen2.5-0.5b as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-7b as the strong student, across 6 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.47 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.67; the LoRA-constrained student trained on weak labels reached a transfer accuracy of 0.56 (SE 0.03), corresponding to a PGR of 0.43 with a standard error of 0.13. The baseline PGR is 0.26, so the observed difference falls within two standard errors of the baseline and cannot be treated as an improvement on this evidence; the direction is favorable but the spread across seeds is wide relative to the gap. With only 6 seeds and a PGR standard error of 0.13, these numbers are best read as suggestive, and a larger seed count would be needed to resolve whether the low-rank restriction helps.
